ev.q: Weekly estimates of variant proportions during January 2, 2022–May 13, 2023, identified the emergence and subsequent predominance of multiple Omicron lineages
The prevalence of these lineages peaked at 75.7% (95% CI = 73.8%–77.5%) for BA.1.1 by the week ending February 19, 2022
The number of cases attributed to each lineage was highest for BA.1.1 (14 million)
the fastest doubling times were observed for XBB.1.16 (15.7 days; 95% CI = 13.9–17.9)
The fastest doubling times among lineages assessed at 1% prevalence during January 2, 2022–May 13, 2023, occurred for BA.2.12.1
CDC’s national genomic surveillance system integrates SARS-CoV-2 sequences from three sources
The weekly number of sequenced specimens decreased from approximately 65,000 collected in January 2022 to approximately 4,400 in April 2023
Biweekly estimates using the updated model were compared with weekly estimates from the previous model to assess consistency.

methods_quotes.q: All methods included weighting to account for the complex survey design and adjust for potential sampling biases.
To estimate variant proportions for the most recent 3 weeks, nowcasts were generated using multinomial regression fit on the previous 21 weeks of data.
Doubling times for proportions of specific lineages were estimated from the coefficients of the multinomial nowcasting model.
Biweekly estimates using the updated model were compared with weekly estimates from the previous model to assess consistency.
